target: def Target : Prop := ∀ T : Set Form, Def15 T (neg (ex 1 Def17))

translation: Target is the proposition that for every set of formulas T (with no restriction on T), the formula neg (ex 1 (all 0 (iff (K (neg (atom 0 0 0))) (atom 0 1 0)))) is derivable from T in the deductive system Def15. Here formulas (Form) are built from binary atomic formulas atom r x y (indexed by natural-number relation symbol r and variable names x, y), falsum (fls), implication (imp), universal quantification (all x), and a unary modal operator K, with negation (neg φ := imp φ fls), conjunction (and φ ψ := neg (imp φ (neg ψ))), biconditional (iff φ ψ := and (imp φ ψ) (imp ψ φ)), and existential quantification (ex x φ := neg (all x (neg φ))) defined as abbreviations. Thus the derived formula states (using relation symbol 0 and variables 0 and 1): ¬∃1 ∀0 (K(¬R₀(0, 0)) ↔ R₀(1, 0)). Derivability from T (Def15 T) is defined inductively as the smallest set of formulas containing every member of T, containing every axiom in Def14, and closed under modus ponens (from imp φ ψ and φ, derive ψ); there are no separate inference rules for generalization or necessitation in Def15. The axiom set Def14 consists of all closed formulas (having no free variables, Def13) obtained by applying zero or more universal quantifiers (Def12) to the base axioms (Def11), together with all formulas of the form K ψ where ψ is such a closed universal closure of a base axiom (so necessitation is built in only as a single outer K on closed universal closures of base axioms). The base axioms (Def11) are: (1) all propositional tautologies (formulas true under every truth assignment v : Form → Prop with ¬v fls and v (imp φ ψ) ↔ (v φ → v ψ)); (2) universal instantiation imp (all x φ) (Def7 x y φ), where Def7 x y φ replaces free occurrences of x with y, subject to the side condition Def8 y x φ that y is free for x in φ (no free occurrence of x lies within the scope of all y); (3) quantifier distribution imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ)); (4) vacuous quantification imp φ (all x φ) whenever x does not occur free in φ; (5) modal distribution imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ)); (6) imp (K φ) φ; (7) imp (K φ) (K (K φ)); and (8) imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ)). Note that Def18 is defined in the context but does not appear in Target.

divergences.description: Target omits the outer modal operator K (Reinhardt's B) governing the universal quantifier: Def17 is ∀0 (K(¬R₀(0,0)) ↔ R₀(1,0)) and Target asserts ∀ T, Def15 T (neg (ex 1 Def17)), i.e. ¬∃e ∀x (B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)), instead of ¬∃e B∀x (B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)) as in Reinhardt's Theorem 5 (and the author's claim) or ¬∃e ∀x B(B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)) as in Reinhardt's proof. Dropping this K produces a strictly stronger and in fact false/unprovable statement in the formal system (∃e ∀x (K¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)) is satisfiable in a two-world reflexive-transitive constant-domain Kripke model validating all axioms in Def14).

Reinhardt's Theorem 5 states the inconsistency of a schema ∃e B∀x(Bp(x) ↔ Uex) where p(x) and U(e,x) are arbitrary formulas, whereas Target fixes the single instance p(x) := ¬U(x,x) and restricts U to a single binary atomic relation symbol (Def16, atom 0). Both restrictions are acknowledged in the author's claim, and the single instance p(x) := ¬U(x,x) suffices to refute the schema, though restricting U from an arbitrary two-variable formula to an atomic relation symbol narrows the statement.

Reinhardt's formal system in P-R323 is built over the language and axioms of arithmetic (with equality, constants, function symbols, and arithmetic axioms optionally prefixed by B), whereas the Lean formalization uses a pure relational logic with only binary relation symbols and no equality or arithmetic axioms. This limitation is declared separately in the author's claim; dropping arithmetic axioms does not weaken an inconsistency claim, though the language cannot express arithmetical formulas for U or p.

judgement.summary: The Lean formalization diverges fatally from Reinhardt's Theorem 5 by omitting the modal operator K (B) in front of the universal quantifier in Def17/Target, formalizing ¬∃e ∀x (B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)) instead of ¬∃e B∀x (B¬U(x,x) ↔ U(e,x)). That omission turns the theorem into an unprovable (false) statement in the defined deductive system.
